text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two presidential decrees are issued. One reduces tariffs on electrical goods by five percent and the other adjusts import duties on finished goods. The reductions will be applied to customs on refrigerators, cookers, televisions and excludes passenger cars and trucks. The two decrees aim to encourage investment, update industry and to make the market adjust to the global economic scene.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said that it has been decided to sell the assets of 15 companies to about 25,000 employees. This will be done over a period of 10 to 20 years. It has also been decided to sell off the public sector cinemas and the film studios will also be sold off but only to Egyptians.

- Tunis and Egypt say that Israel is responsible for stalling the Middle East peace process. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa delivered a letter from President Hosni Mubarak to Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali.
- Government to revaluate the wages and incentives given to civil servants to improve their lifestyle.

- Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif says the Egyptian satellite Nilesat will be launched next January. The satellite has a total of 12 channels capable of handling broadcasts from 84 television stations. The private sector has bought 60 percent of these channels and the rest are owned by the Egyptian Radio and Television Union.

- Public Enterprise Minister Obeid says the government, under the directives of President Mubarak, will offer to privatise 10 firms every three months. Obeid says the state is also negotiating with Danish and Norwegian firms to restructure some public firms and will offer a "basket" of hotels at an investment conference to be held in Cairo in September.
- Moussa says there is still a chance to save the peace process.
- Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali says that the cotton crop is in excellent condition and the higher temperatures bode well for a big harvest.
- Prosecutor to announce details of the investigation which began after Alaa and Gamal Mubarak complained about articles written in Asharq al-Awsat newspaper.
- Moussa: Egypt demands that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stop building settlements immediately.
